sections.title: Advanced Concept
sections.content: Level 3 deals with complex average problems: multiple groups, successive changes, weighted replacements, and multi-step real-life scenarios. Problems often require logical setup and indirect calculations.

sections.title: Successive Changes in Average
sections.content: When numbers are added or removed one after another, calculate stepwise. New average = (Previous sum ± new numbers)/new count. Example: Avg of 5 numbers = 20 → Add 25 → New avg = 21 → Remove 15 → New avg = (21×6 - 15)/5 = 23.2.

sections.title: Complex Weighted Averages
sections.content: When combining multiple groups with different sizes and averages, calculate sum for each group, sum all, then divide by total count. Example: Group A (8 students avg 50), B (10 students avg 60), C (12 students avg 55) → Combined avg = (8×50 + 10×60 +12×55)/30 = 55.33.

sections.title: Replacement of Multiple Observations
sections.content: If more than one number is replaced, calculate total sum difference = sum of new numbers - sum of replaced numbers, then add to old sum and divide by total count. Example: Avg of 6 numbers = 40 → Replace 30, 50 with 35, 45 → New avg = (40×6 + (35+45) - (30+50))/6 = 40.

sections.title: Average of Numbers in Ratio
sections.content: If numbers are in ratio, average can be calculated by finding one term and summing proportionally. Example: Numbers in 2:3:5 → Let total sum = 100 → Numbers = 20,30,50 → Avg = 100/3 ≈ 33.33.

sections.title: Successive Group Mergers
sections.content: When multiple groups are merged stepwise, calculate combined sum after each merge, not directly. Example: Merge 3 groups of 5, 10, 15 students with avg 40,50,60 → Merge 1&2 → Temp sum = 5×40+10×50=700 → Temp count=15 → Temp avg=46.67 → Merge with 3 → New avg=(700+15×60)/30 = 51.67.

sections.title: Using Deviations from Known Average
sections.content: Sum of deviations helps in solving tricky replacement/addition problems quickly. Example: Avg = 20 → Deviations from avg: -5, 0, 5 → Remove -5, add 10 → New avg = 20 + (10 - (-5))/3 = 25/3 ≈ 8.33 increment.

sections.title: Real-Life Applications
sections.content: Used in performance analysis, production output, mark calculations, or financial averages. Problems often combine several steps: merging, replacements, scaling, and additions.

tricks.title: Successive Change Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Update sum and count stepwise for each addition/removal.

tricks.title: Multiple Replacements Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Sum difference = sum of new numbers - sum of replaced numbers; add to total sum, divide by count.

tricks.title: Weighted Average of Multiple Groups
tricks.explanation: Sum each group separately (avg × size), then divide by total count.

tricks.title: Average Using Ratios
tricks.explanation: If numbers in ratio a:b:c, assign values proportional to sum or given condition.

tricks.title: Deviation Method for Quick Calculation
tricks.explanation: Use deviations from average to quickly compute effect of changes.

tricks.title: Merging Groups Stepwise
tricks.explanation: Merge two groups at a time to avoid calculation errors in multiple groups.
tricks.example: Merge group1&2 → temp avg → merge with group3 → final avg.

tricks.title: Scaling Trick
tricks.explanation: Multiply all numbers by k → new avg = old avg × k.

tricks.title: Additive Constant Trick
tricks.explanation: Add constant c to all numbers → new avg = old avg + c.

tricks.title: Checking Using Sum of Deviations
tricks.explanation: Sum of deviations from average = 0 → helps verify multi-step problems.

tricks.title: Quick Estimation
tricks.explanation: Round numbers or use approximate ratios to get close average quickly.
